workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder was charged £54.00 twice by Roastline Coffee Co on 12 April 2025 for a single purchase. To defend, the merchant must show both charges were separate purchases, document each purchase event, and provide the timestamp and authorisation code for each charge. All three requirements must be met.

requirements.reasoning: The two invoices carry different order IDs and different items: coffee beans on Order A, and an Aeropress kit with filter papers on Order B. They reached the same £54.00 by different routes: Order A was £60.00 less a £6.00 loyalty discount, Order B was £54.00 with no discount.

Each purchase has its own invoice number, delivery date and DPD consignment number. The delivery details are stated on the merchant's invoices rather than on carrier proof of delivery, but separate invoices on their own meet this requirement.
Each charge has a distinct authorisation code and a capture timestamp roughly 11.5 hours apart.

workup.action_justification: All three requirements are satisfied: two distinct orders with separate invoices, items, auth codes, timestamps and DPD consignments.
workup.rationale: The cardholder was charged twice on 12 April 2025 for two separate orders, not one transaction processed twice. Order RL-ORDER-44188 (invoice RL-88291, auth code 442189, captured 08:11:33) was for coffee beans totalling £60.00 less a £6.00 loyalty discount. Order RL-ORDER-44192 (invoice RL-88294, auth code 552781, captured 19:42:18) was for an Aeropress Go starter kit and filter papers totalling £54.00. The orders were shipped as separate DPD consignments (7711224488 and 7711224501) to the cardholder's verified address, N1 4PD, and delivered on 14 and 15 April respectively. The disputed transaction passed AVS, CVV and frictionless 3DS.
caveats: Timezone mismatch: the transaction record shows 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z (UTC), but invoice A states 08:11:33 BST, which is 07:11:33 UTC. Confirm which clock is correct and that the disputed txn_5523IJ corresponds to auth code 442189 (Order A).
Confirm in acquirer records that both auth codes (442189 and 552781) exist as separate settled transactions on this card. The case metadata identifies only one transaction.

Delivery dates and DPD tracking numbers come from the merchant's invoices, not carrier records. They are not required to satisfy the rule, but DPD proof of delivery would strengthen the file if the issuer pre-arbitrates.

Invoice B contains a merchant-written note asserting 'Both charges are valid.' This is the merchant's conclusion and was given no weight. The assessment rests on the order IDs, items, auth codes and timestamps.

rule_text:
Visa 12.6.1 - Duplicate Processing
Issuer claim: The same transaction was processed more than once.
Logic: ALL 3 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered)
  2. Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates)
  3. Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: frictionless
Chargeback raised 18 days after the transaction
